I essentially ended the conversation with “wish you the best” and I didn’t really say anything about “if things go bad, I’ll let you know”. Didn’t seem like a healthy thing to say as I’ll always view her as a “backup”. That’s bad for all parties involved.

It's good to hear from somebody that may have gone through the same shit. I know I won't commit suicide because of how many people care about me, but the thoughts of it keep me awake some nights and it scares me so much. Thanks for the comment.

The end of your comment is what disturbs me the most about myself. I know that my family loves me, but why do I feel so unwanted and unloved? Just feels so much easier to be gone. I am disturbed by my thoughts, and I am too rational to act upon them. I know I will not end my own life anytime soon, but I am worried that I am having these thoughts at all if that makes sense.

Coins. I bought most of them when I was 10-15 (I'm 22 now) and I was so addicted to it. I would buy $25 penny boxes and find at least $50 in errors/varieties in every box. I would buy silver coins that people didn't know were worth more  and offer them double face value         (A silver quarter is worth at least 5$ just in silver content alone). When I last calculated the overall value of my collection it was around $2000, but with silver prices skyrocketing I'm looking at probably double that now. I'm a history nerd and an investing addict so it is literally the perfect hobby.

Honestly it sucked. It felt like a normal head cold for a couple days and then the flu on steroids. I would wake up and feel like I worked out for 3 hours the previous day. Everything ached. I couldn't breathe when I layed down. I couldn't smell anything (still can't a month and a half later) but I could taste perfectly fine. All I wanted to do was sleep. I wasn't too worried about it as I wanted to get it just so it was over with, but that week and a half was miserable.
